policy.definition: An Operational Exception is a defect, limitation, or gap in a third-party component, external dependency, or upstream runtime that does not reflect a deficiency in Open Empire's own implementation architecture.
policy.separation_principle: Open Empire-owned work is assessed independently of third-party runtime defects.
policy.certification_rule: A Track certification is not held open solely because of upstream runtime defects that have documented workarounds and do not compromise governance integrity, registry integrity, trading safety, or data integrity.
policy.escalation: Operational Exceptions are tracked and resolved in Track C — Autonomous Operations & Production Hardening.

exceptions.title: n8n v2.8.4 fails to bind on port 5678 after pm2 restart
exceptions.description: n8n v2.8.4 enters a hang state after pm2 restart on macOS 12.7.6 (x64). Process starts, emits 'Initializing n8n process' and 'Error tracking disabled because this release is older than 6 weeks', then stops without binding to port 5678. This is a version-specific defect in n8n v2.8.4 — the original process (pid=771) ran continuously for 4+ days without issue. The defect manifests only on restart.
exceptions.business_impact: OEPM webhook endpoints (runtime-health-alert, governance-change, registry-mutation, deploy-validation, budget-alert, repo-registration) are not reachable until n8n is restarted correctly. Existing Telegram alerts via direct channel remain operational.
